rawInci: Ingredients: Aqua, Sodium Laureth Sulfate, Cocamidopropyl Betaine, Sodium Chloride, Argania Spinosa Kernel Oil, Orbignya Oleifera Seed Oil, Sclerocarya Birrea Seed Oil, Parfum, Glycerin, Propylene Glycol, Laureth-4, PEG-40 Hydrogenated Castor Oil, Glycol Distearate, PEG-4 Rapeseedamide, Disodium Cocoyl Glutamate, Sodium Cocoyl Glutamate, Guar Hydroxypropyltrimonium Chloride, Hydrolyzed Keratin, Sodium Benzoate, Potassium Sorbate, Benzoic Acid, Tetramethyl Acetyloctahydronaphthalenes, Citric Acid, Sodium Hydroxide

propertyRationales.cleansingStrength: SLES is the lead cleanser with betaine and glutamate co-surfactants, so cleansing is strong despite the refatting/oil load.
propertyRationales.conditioningLevel: Three oils plus cationic guar and hydrolyzed keratin create a plausible non-silicone conditioning system, but rinse-off delivery and exact deposition are uncertain.
propertyRationales.weightPotential: The cationic polymer route is substantive, but the oils are treated as weak-to-moderate rather than clearly substantive because this is a surfactant-rich rinse-off shampoo without a clear oil-deposition carrier; therefore the exact v1.4 two-substantive-route threshold for high is not met.
propertyRationales.focusPrimary: Blind formula alone shows a care-leaning shampoo, but without claims it does not force a single dominant focus beyond general.
propertyRationales.focusSecondary: No secondary focus is assigned because v1.4 defaults to empty without distinct positioning signals.
propertyRationales.usageRole: No frequent, reset, clarifying or treatment trigger is available from formula-only input, so v1.4 default regular applies.
propertyRationales.scalpComfortTarget: The formula has some amphoteric and refatting moderation, but SLES, fragrance and no tolerance evidence mean scalp comfort is not formula-targeted.
propertyRationales.dandruffSupport: The complete formula does not list Piroctone Olamine or Climbazole.

formulaObservations: SLES appears second, followed by Cocamidopropyl Betaine and salt.
Three botanical oils appear before fragrance, suggesting a meaningful oil/refatting signal for a rinse-off shampoo.
Guar Hydroxypropyltrimonium Chloride supplies a cationic polymer deposition route.
Hydrolyzed Keratin is present late and should be treated as weak surface-film support.
No silicone or recognized anti-dandruff active is listed.
counterSignals: Oil deposition from rinse-off shampoo is uncertain without finished-formula evidence.
Strong SLES-led cleansing may reduce perceived softness and reset some residue.
Glycol Distearate can pearlize the product and should not be counted alone as hair shine.
Citric Acid alone does not establish finished acidic pH.

finalDelta.reason: Der unblindete Oil-Repair-Kontext passt zur Formel: drei Pflanzenöle vor Parfum, kationisches Guar und Keratin stützen ein hohes, nicht-silikonisches Pflege-/Depositionspotenzial im Shampoo.
Nach v1.4 zählen der frühe Ölkomplex und kationisches Guar als zwei unterschiedliche substantive Depositionsrouten; deshalb ist das Beschwerungspotenzial hoch, auch wenn die Reinigung stark ist.
Die dominierende Oil-Repair-/Trockenhaar-Positionierung ist formelkompatibel über Öl, kationisches Guar und Keratin; Repair beschreibt hier temporäre kosmetische Pflege, keine echte Strukturheilung.

focusPrimary.formulaRoute: Ölkomplex vor Parfum plus kationisches Guar und Keratin stützen temporäre Pflege/Repair-Oberflächenwirkung.
focusPrimary.decisionReason: Der Name und die offiziellen Claims sind klar Oil-Repair-led; die Formel ist damit kompatibel.

usageRole.rationale: Normale Shampooanwendung; kein Reset-, Daily-non-strong- oder Active-Problem-Trigger.

formulaRoutes.evidence: Argan-, Babassu- und Marulaöl stehen vor Parfum als zusammenhängender Öl-/Refatting-Komplex.
Guar Hydroxypropyltrimonium Chloride ist eine wirksame kationische Depositionsroute auch bei niedriger Einsatzmenge.
Hydrolyzed Keratin ergänzt Repair-/Film-Support nur schwach.

competingSignals: SLES-led cleansing can reduce perceived coating but does not cancel deposition routes.
